preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly two lines.
The first line contains an integer n representing the length of the string, where 1 <= n <= 100.

preconditions.expression: len(lines[1].strip()) == int(lines[0]) and all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in lines[1].strip())
preconditions.description: The second line contains a string s of length n consisting only of lowercase Latin letters.

postconditions.description: The output is a single non-negative integer.

The output integer equals the maximum number of characters that can be removed from s by optimally choosing a sequence of valid operations, where a character can be removed if it has an adjacent character that is the previous letter in the alphabet.
